lessons.title: 1. Key-Value Lookup & Safe Retrieval (`.get()`)
lessons.description: Finish `get_item_count(inventory, item)`. Return how many of `item` are in the dictionary, or `0` when the key is missing. Use `.get` so a missing key does not crash. For `{"apple": 10}`, apple is `10` and orange is `0`. The test checks that `get_item_count(inv, "apple")` equals `10`; `get_item_count(inv, "orange")` equals `0`.
learning_objectives: Access and assign dictionary keys and use .get()

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — Mapping Types — dict.get() (Standard Types)

lessons.title: 2. Iterating Over Dictionaries (`.items()`, `del`)
lessons.description: Finish `total_inventory_count(inventory)` so it returns the sum of every stored count. `total_inventory_count({"a": 5, "b": 15})` equals `20`. The test checks that `total_inventory_count({"a": 5, "b": 15})` equals `20`.

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — 5.5. Dictionaries — Data Structures (view objects)

lessons.title: 3. Inventory Management (Concept Challenge)
lessons.description: Finish `create_inventory`, `add_items`, `decrement_items`, `remove_item` and 1 more. Create and mutate store inventory using dictionary methods. The test checks that `create_inventory(['coal', 'wood', 'wood'])` equals `{'coal': 1, 'wood': 2}`; `add_items({'wood': 4, 'iron': 1}, ['wood', 'iron', 'diamond'])` equals `{'wood': 5, 'iron': 2, 'diamond': 1}`; `decrement_items({'wood': 2, 'iron': 1}, ['wood', 'wood', 'wood', 'iron'])` equals `{'wood': 0, 'iron': 0}`.
learning_objectives: Use .get() and dict assignment to update counts

lessons.title: 4. Word Frequency Counter (Practice)
lessons.description: Finish `count_words`. Count word occurrences in a list using a dictionary. The test checks that `count_words(["a", "b", "a"])` equals `{"a": 2, "b": 1}`.

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — 5.5. Dictionaries — Data Structures

lessons.title: 5. Unit 12 Checkpoint: Dictionaries Mastery
lessons.description: Finish `merge_inventories(inv1, inv2)`. Return a new dictionary with the counts from both inventories added together. Do not change the originals. `merge_inventories({"a": 2}, {"a": 3, "b": 4})` equals `{"a": 5, "b": 4}`. The test checks that `merge_inventories({"a": 2}, {"a": 3, "b": 4})` equals `{"a": 5, "b": 4}`.

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — 5.5. Dictionaries — Data Structures
